## Learning objectives 
<div style="font-size: 150%;">

1. Understand the statement of the CLT
2. Use the CLT to answer a public health question

</div>
  
---

# Question: what is the average daily caffeine consumption among Americans? 

# How might we answer this question? 

# We could survey every single American 

::: {.notes}
But this is impractical (impossible?) and expensive
:::

# We could take a sample 
::: {.notes}
Have person 1 take a sample
::: 


---

### Sample one person 


```{r s1}
#| cache: true 


set.seed(123)
s1 = caffeine_df %>% 
  slice_sample(n=1)

s1 %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(40),
    heading.title.font.size = px(50),
    column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
    table.align = "left",
    table.width = pct(70),
    quarto.use_bootstrap = TRUE
  ) %>% 
  cols_align("left",
             columns = everything())
```


---

### Add another person to sample and calculate average


```{r s2}
#| cache: true
set.seed(1234)
s2 = caffeine_df %>% 
  slice_sample(n=1)

s1 %>% 
  bind_rows(s2) %>% 
  mutate(cumulative_sample_mean = cummean(caffeine_mg)) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(40),
    heading.title.font.size = px(50),
    column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
    table.align = "left",
    table.width = pct(100)
  ) %>% 
  cols_align("left",
             columns = everything())
```


---

### Add more people to sample

```{r s3}
#| cache: true
set.seed(1235)
s3 = caffeine_df %>% 
  slice_sample(n=28)

s1 %>% 
  bind_rows(s2) %>% 
  bind_rows(s3) %>% 
  mutate(cumulative_sample_mean = cummean(caffeine_mg)) %>% 
  slice(1:10) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(40),
    heading.title.font.size = px(50),
    column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
    table.align = "left",
    table.width = pct(100)
  ) %>% 
  cols_align("left",
             columns = everything())
```

### Lily's sample

```{r}
#| cache: true
samp_df = 
  s1 %>% 
  bind_rows(s2) %>% 
  bind_rows(s3) %>% 
  mutate(cumulative_sample_mean = cummean(caffeine_mg)) %>% 
  mutate(n = row_number())

samp_df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = cumulative_sample_mean)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 130)) +
  labs(x = "Number of people in sample", y = "Sample mean caffeine (mg)", title = "n = 30")


```

### How do the samples compare? 


```{r}

  samp_df2 %>% 
  mutate(name = "Lily's Sample") %>%

  ggplot(aes(x= n, y = cumulative_sample_mean, color = name)) +
```

```{r}

n_sims = 100

  map_dfr(.x = 1:n_sims,

            set.seed(sim + 1232)
            df = caffeine_df %>% 
              slice_sample(n=100) %>%
```

# Interactive 

---

```{ojs}
data = FileAttachment("caffeine_df.csv").csv({ typed: true })

viewof sample_size = Inputs.range(
  [2, 200], 
  {value: 50, step: 1, label: "Sample size:"}
)



sample_means = {
  // Dependency tracking: re-run when these change
  sample_size;
  
  // Safety check: ensure data is loaded
  if (!data || data.length === 0) return [];
  
  // Safety check: ensure column exists (Case Sensitive!)
  if (typeof data[0].caffeine_mg === "undefined") {
    return ["Error: Column 'caffeine_mg' not found in data"];
  }

  const means = [];
  // Create a local copy of the array to shuffle
  // We do this inside the loop or use a specific shuffler to ensure 
  // we are sampling from the full population every time.
  const popArray = Array.from(data); 

  for (let i = 0; i < 500; i++) {
    // 1. Shuffle a clean copy of the population
    // 2. Slice the first n elements (Sampling WITHOUT replacement)
    const sample = d3.shuffle([...popArray]).slice(0, sample_size);

    // 3. Compute mean
    const m = d3.mean(sample, d => d.caffeine_mg);
    means.push(m);
  }

  return means;
}


// 5. CALCULATE NORMAL CURVE (THEORETICAL)
// We now generate the curve based on the Population Parameters, not the sample.
// This shows the Theoretical prediction of the CLT.
normalCurve = {
  if (sample_means.length < 2 || !data) return [];
  
  // 1. Get Population Statistics
  const popMean = d3.mean(data, d => d.caffeine_mg);
  const popSD = d3.deviation(data, d => d.caffeine_mg);
  
  // 2. Calculate Standard Error (The predicted width of the sampling distribution)
  // Formula: Population SD / sqrt(n)
  const se = popSD / Math.sqrt(sample_size);

  // 3. Determine range for the curve (centered on popMean)
  const minX = popMean - (4 * se);
  const maxX = popMean + (4 * se);
  
  // Create a smooth grid of X values
  const grid = d3.range(minX, maxX, (maxX - minX) / 200);
  
  // Normal Density Function using Population Mean and Standard Error
  const pdf = (x) => (1 / (se * Math.sqrt(2 * Math.PI))) * Math.exp(-0.5 * Math.pow((x - popMean) / se, 2));
  
  return grid.map(x => ({x: x, y: pdf(x)}));
}

// 6. PLOT
// 6. SIDE-BY-SIDE PLOTS WITH EXTERNAL LEGEND
{
  // --- A. SETUP VARIABLES ---
  const popMean = d3.mean(data, d => d.caffeine_mg);
  const n = sample_means.length;
  const bins = d3.bin().thresholds(20)(sample_means);
  
  // NEW: Calculate fixed x-axis limits based on the Population Data
  // This ensures the axis stays constant regardless of sample size
  const xLimits = d3.extent(data, d => d.caffeine_mg);
  const xLimits2 = [0, 750];

  // Define colors
  const colorDomain = ["Sampling Distribution Mean", "Population Mean", "Normal Curve"];
  const colorRange = ["black", "#E69F00", "#D55E00"];

  // --- B. POPULATION PLOT (Left) ---
  const popPlot = Plot.plot({
    width: 550,
    height: 500,
    caption: "Population Distribution (Raw Data)",
    marginTop: 40,
    marginLeft: 50,
    marginBottom: 40,
    style: { fontSize: "14px", overflow: "visible" },
    
    marks: [
      Plot.rectY(data, Plot.binX({y: "count"}, {x: "caffeine_mg", fill: "#444444", fillOpacity: 0.5})),
    ],
    // We explicitly set the domain here too, just to be safe and consistent
    x: { label: "Caffeine consumption (mg)", domain: xLimits }, 
    y: { label: "Count" }
  });

  // --- C. SAMPLING DISTRIBUTION PLOT (Right) ---
  const sampPlot = Plot.plot({
    width: 550,
    height: 500,
    caption: `Distribution of sample means at (n=${sample_size})`,
    marginTop: 40,
    marginLeft: 50,
    marginBottom: 40,
    style: { fontSize: "14px", overflow: "visible" },
    
    color: {
      domain: colorDomain,
      range: colorRange,
      legend: false
    },
    marks: [
      Plot.rectY(bins, {
        x1: "x0", x2: "x1", 
        y: d => d.length / (n * (d.x1 - d.x0)), 
        fill: "#444444", fillOpacity: 0.3, tip: true,
        title: d => `Count: ${d.length}\nDensity: ${(d.length / (n * (d.x1 - d.x0))).toFixed(3)}`
      }),
      Plot.line(normalCurve, {x: "x", y: "y", stroke: () => "Normal Curve", strokeWidth: 3}),
      Plot.ruleX([d3.mean(sample_means)], {stroke: () => "Sampling Distribution Mean", strokeWidth: 3}),
      Plot.ruleX([popMean], {stroke: () => "Population Mean", strokeDasharray: "4,4", strokeWidth: 2, opacity: 0.8})
    ],
    // NEW: Apply the fixed population domain here
    // x: { label: "Sample Mean", tickFormat: ".1f", domain: xLimits }, 
    x: { label: "Sample Mean", tickFormat: ".1f", domain: xLimits2 },
    y: { label: "Density" }
  });

  // --- D. LEGEND & LAYOUT ---
  const myLegend = Plot.legend({
    color: { domain: colorDomain, range: colorRange },
    style: { marginBottom: "10px", fontSize: "14px" }
  });

  return html`
  <div style="display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center;">
    <div style="width: 100%; max-width: 920px; display: flex; justify-content: flex-end;">
      ${myLegend}
    </div>
    <div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 20px; justify-content: center;">
      <div>${popPlot}</div>
      <div>${sampPlot}</div>
    </div>
  </div>`;
}
```

## The Central Limit Theorem

::: {.incremental}
<div style="font-size: 130%;">

+ **Reality:**
  + We only get **one** sample and sample mean ($\bar{X}_n$)
  + We *never* know the true population mean $(\mu)$
+ **CLT**: tells us how the single sample mean relates to the unknown truth


</div>
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$\bar{X}_n  \xrightarrow{d} N\left(\mu, \frac{\sigma^2}{n}\right)$$
:::

---

### The Central Limit Theorem


```{r}
#| cache: true 


pop_mean = mean(caffeine_df$caffeine_mg)
pop_var = var(caffeine_df$caffeine_mg)
se = sqrt(pop_var / 100)

x_min = pop_mean - 3.2 * se; x_max = pop_mean + 3.2 * se
pnormal = 
  ggplot(data = tibble(x = seq(x_min, x_max, 0.01)), aes(x)) +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, n = 101, args = list(mean = pop_mean, sd = se), linewidth = 1.1) +
  labs(y = "Density", x = "Sample mean caffeine intake (mg)", title = "Approximate distribution of sample mean when n = 100",
       subtitle = "By CLT") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(60, 180, 10))

pnormal
```

### The Central Limit Theorem


```{r}
#| cache: true 


pop_mean = mean(caffeine_df$caffeine_mg)
pop_var = var(caffeine_df$caffeine_mg)
se = sqrt(pop_var / 100)

x_min = pop_mean - 3.2 * se; x_max = pop_mean + 3.2 * se
pnormal2 = 
  pnormal +
  geom_labelvline(aes(xintercept = pop_mean), color = "#E69F00", 
                  label = glue::glue("Mean = pop. mean = {round(pop_mean, 0)} mg")) + 
  annotate(geom = "segment",          color = "#444444",
           x = pop_mean + se / 2, xend = pop_mean, y = 0.01, yend = 0.01,
          arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "inches"), type = "closed")) +
  annotate(geom = "segment",          color = "#444444",
           x = pop_mean + se / 2, xend = pop_mean + se, y = 0.01, yend = 0.01,
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "inches"), type = "closed")) +
  annotate(geom = "label",
         x = pop_mean + se / 2,
         color = "#444444",
         y = 0.007,
         # Use expression() to wrap the math logic
         label = expression(atop(
           # Top line: Formula
           SD == frac("Population SD", sqrt(n)),
           # Bottom line: Substitution
           phantom(SD) == frac(166, sqrt(100))
         ))) 
pnormal2
```

# If we only observe one sample, how can we actually make a statement about the population? 

# Teaser for next time: inference (confidence intervals) 

---

### Using the CLT to quantify uncertainty: confidence intervals 

```{r}
#| cache: true

# Let's focus on Sample 1 (Pink)
sample_val = vals[1]
ci_lower = sample_val - 1.96 * se
ci_upper = sample_val + 1.96 * se

# Re-create the plot but make the Truth (Orange Line) faint/dashed to show it's "unknown"
p_inference = 
  ggplot(data = tibble(x = seq(x_min, x_max, 0.01)), aes(x)) +
  # Faint "Truth" distribution
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, n = 101, args = list(mean = pop_mean, sd = se), 
                color = "darkgrey", linetype = "dashed") +
  # The Truth Line (Faint)
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = pop_mean), color = "#E69F00", linetype = "dotted", alpha = 0.75) +
  # The Sample Dot
  annotate(geom = "point", x = sample_val, y = 0, color = "#CC79A7", size = 5) +
  # The Confidence Interval "Net"
  annotate(geom = "segment", x = ci_lower, xend = ci_upper, y = 0, yend = 0,
           color = "#CC79A7", linewidth = 1.2) +
  # Error Bar whiskers
  annotate(geom = "segment", x = ci_lower, xend = ci_lower, y = -0.001, yend = 0.001,
           color = "#CC79A7", linewidth = 1.2) +
  annotate(geom = "segment", x = ci_upper, xend = ci_upper, y = -0.001, yend = 0.001,
           color = "#CC79A7", linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(y = "", x = "Caffeine (mg)") +
  annotate(geom = "text", x = sample_val, y = 0.002, label = "Lily's Sample Mean", color = "#CC79A7", vjust = 0) +
  annotate(geom = "text", x = pop_mean, y = 0.002, label = "True Population Mean", color = "#E69F00", vjust = 0) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, color = "#444444"))

p_inference
```
